ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, and points $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$ are on the same line, with $CG=CD$, $DF=DE$. What is the measure of $\angle E$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore, $\angle ACB=60^\circ$,\\
since CG=CD,\\
therefore, $\angle CDG=\angle CGD=30^\circ$,\\
since DF=DE,\\
therefore, $\angle E=\angle DFE=\boxed{15^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, B, C, D, E are on the same horizontal straight line, in the order B, C, D, E; △ABC is drawn on the left side, A is above, and there is point G on side AC; from G it is connected to D toward the lower right, and point F is located on segment DG; from F it is connected to E toward the lower right. The problem gives that △ABC is an equilateral triangle, and CG=CD, DF=DE. Reasoning: Because △ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠ACB=60°. In the figure, G is on AC, D is on the right side of C, and CD is the reverse extension line of CB, therefore ∠GCD=180°−60°=120°. In △CGD, CG=CD, so it is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠CDG and ∠CGD are equal, each being (180°−120°)/2=30°. Also because F is on DG, and E is on the same straight line on the right side of D, ∠FDE and ∠CDG are supplementary, ∠FDE=180°−30°=150°. In △DFE, DF=DE, so the base angles ∠DFE and ∠E are equal, therefore ∠E=(180°−150°)/2=15°.
